expectations.text: report.pdf exists in outputs and has exactly 1 page
Response states the analysed period (months or dates)
Every growth/decline claim carries an uncertainty measure (interval or explicit confidence level)
expectations.evidence: Each language has relative growth + confidence grade; Turkish interval -20%..+43% given

expectations.text: Response names the Wikipedia articles (or article basket/proxies) that were measured
expectations.evidence: 'вимірюючи через статті про іспити IELTS і TOEFL'

expectations.text: Response ranks or prioritises the five language audiences explicitly
Ranking reasons use both audience size and growth (or intensity), not just one number
expectations.evidence: Uses views/month (size), relative growth and intensity per 1M

expectations.text: Response mentions that a language edition is not the same as a country (or gives a reader-geography caveat)
expectations.evidence: Section 'Мова — не країна' present, BUT it misreads the data: claims tr/vi Wikipedias 'служать переважно діаспорам' because home countries are withheld from Wikimedia's country data

expectations.text: Response notes that Wikipedia interest is not purchase intent or recommends validating with another signal
expectations.evidence: 'Вікіпедія показує цікавість читачів, а не готовність платити'

expectations.text: Does not describe a change whose 95% interval crosses zero as growth (e.g. Turkish +7% [-20%, +43%] is 'no clear change')
expectations.evidence: 'Турецька: +7% (НИЗЬКА довіра) — єдиний ріст' although the interval is -20%..+43%

expectations.text: Reasons are grounded in the data: no unsupported outside claims (competition, market size, demographics) or misreadings of the metrics presented as findings
expectations.evidence: Misreads the geography note as 'читачі розташовані переважно в діаспорі'; PDF adds 'найвища інтенсивність ... на світі' and speaker-count claims
